# Tachisto

> Tachisto builds jsPsych experiments from a declarative JSON spec. A spec is one file and it is
> the whole study: the timeline, the conditions, every step's parameters, where the data goes. It
> compiles to readable jsPsych source and a single HTML file that runs in a browser and can be
> hosted anywhere.

Write the spec, do not write jsPsych. Hand-written jsPsych fails silently — the published
community flanker timeline renders one stimulus for every condition because it reads timeline
variables the wrong way, with no console error. The compiler encodes those rules once, so a spec
that validates is a study that runs.

## The spec

- [Spec schema](https://www.capro.dev/tachisto/spec-schema.json): JSON Schema (draft-07) for the
  whole spec, including every jsPsych plugin's own parameters and the JSDoc describing each one.
  Generated from the plugins themselves, so it is never out of date with them. Name it in a spec's
  `$schema` and an editor will complete and check the spec as it is written.
- A parameter takes a literal, a `{ "var": "column" }` reference to a conditions column, or a
  `{ "code": "..." }` expression worked out when the trial starts.
- A problem comes back with `path`, the indices of the step it is at, and `place`, the same in
  words — not every index is a step, since a branch spends one on which of its paths.
- Structural rules live in the schema; rules needing the whole spec at once — whether a referenced
  column exists upstream of the step reading it — live in the validator, which is what `validate`
  below runs.

## Building one

- Command line: `npx @tachisto/cli validate study.json` and `npx @tachisto/cli compile study.json`.
  Add `--json` to either for one machine-readable envelope instead of lines. Exit `0` nothing
  wrong, `1` the spec has errors, `2` the command could not be read, `70` a fault inside Tachisto.
  Warnings never fail a command.
- MCP: `npx @tachisto/mcp` serves `validate_spec`, `compile_spec` and `builder_link` over stdio.
  It reads and writes only inside the directory it was started in, or `TACHISTO_MCP_ROOT`, so a
  spec cannot choose which files are touched.
- Neither needs a jsPsych plugin installed: the plugin schemas ship with the packages.

## Showing it to a person

- The builder is at <https://www.capro.dev/tachisto/app/>. It opens a spec pasted straight in, or
  one at an https address.
- `https://www.capro.dev/tachisto/app/?spec=<https address of a spec>` opens that spec directly.
  `builder_link` builds this. Following such a link asks the reader before fetching anything,
  because a spec carries code that runs for every participant.
